step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates OLX Autos' internal developer platform ('Orion portal') architecture. First, DNS resolution for requests targeting the portal is handled by Amazon Route 53, which resolves to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB routes incoming requests to Kubernetes pods managed by Amazon EKS running on 100% EC2 Spot instances. When environment provisioning jobs are created for various microservices, EKS jobs publish status events to Amazon SNS. SNS fans out these messages to Amazon SQS. If a Spot instance is terminated mid-job, replacement jobs running on EC2 Spot instances watch SQS for unfinished job state events to resume and complete microservice deployment.

graph.name: OLX Autos Developer Platform Architecture
graph.notes: OLX Autos architecture using 100% EC2 Spot instances managed by Amazon EKS, resiliently handling spot terminations using SNS and SQS for state tracking.

nodes.name: ROUTE 53
nodes.notes: Handles DNS resolution for incoming requests to the Orion portal.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Application Load Balancer that routes web traffic to EKS pods.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Amazon EKS container orchestrator running over 10,000 pods to manage microservices.

nodes.name: SPOT
nodes.notes: 100% EC2 Spot instances hosting pods and microservices, monitored by AWS Node Termination Handler.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Publishes events whenever microservice deployment jobs are triggered.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Stores job state messages fanned out from SNS to track unfinished tasks.

edges.notes: Route 53 resolves DNS domain to the Application Load Balancer.
ALB routes incoming user requests to EKS pods.
ALB directs traffic to workloads on EC2 Spot instances.
EKS microservice provisioning jobs send execution events to SNS.
SNS fans out state message events to the SQS queue.
Replacement jobs running on Spot instances watch SQS for unfinished tasks and complete them.
